title: TF compatibility policy and pinlist for Private VPC deployments
creator: Avery Chen
description: Create an auditable compatibility policy and canonical version pinlist for Terraform providers and internal TF modules used by Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. Deliverables: a machine-readable pinlist, upgrade compatibility matrix, automated health-check and canary test harness, and a GitHub Actions workflow that enforces pins and runs pre-merge checks for upgrade PRs.
acceptance_criteria: Published pinlist file (json/csv) in infra/repos/tf-pinning with entries for providers and all internal modules used by private deployments
Compatibility matrix document mapping module versions to minimum compatible provider versions and runtime flags
A GitHub Actions workflow that fails CI for changes that introduce unapproved provider/module bumps without a valid compatibility entry
Automated canary job in CI that applies changes to an isolated test VPC and runs health checks (KV cache, TLS, routing, rollout hooks)
PR template and runbook for upgrade PRs that includes rollback steps and test results
decisions: Adopt a single source-of-truth JSON pinlist (infra/tf/pinlist.json) that is authoritative for apply pipelines and release engineers
Provider pinning granularity will be provider:major.minor.patch and module pinning will be semver with explicit allowed-bump ranges (e.g., ~1.2.x allowed for patch updates)
All provider bumps must include: upgrade tests, module compatibility confirmation, and a security review sign-off if provider major version changes
We will tolerate patch-level provider upgrades automatically if the compatibility matrix indicates 'auto-patch: true' and CI tests pass
Rollbacks will be automatic via terraform state pin/force-replace playbook and documented in the upgrade PR
automation_playbook: GH Actions + terraform CLI: pre-merge plan, isolated apply to canary VPC (ephemeral), run health_checks.sh, report results to PR and Slack #infra-upgrades
rollout_plan: 1) Create/update pinlist in feature branch. 2) Create upgrade PR referencing compatibility matrix and test outputs. 3) CI runs plan + canary apply. 4) If canary passes, schedule staged rollout to dedicated testbed pools, then production Dedicated clusters. 5) Monitor runtime metrics for 48 hours; auto rollback on critical errors.

2026-02-25 Riley Morgan (Security): Recommended running provider upgrade tests under KMS-backed secrets and adding artifact signing for the pinlist — added to scope.

notes: This ticket composes several artifacts: pinlist schema (JSON), compatibility matrix (Confluence + csv export), GH Actions workflow, canary apply scripts, and PR templates. Keep the pinlist minimal and authoritative to avoid drift between repos.
implementation_tasks: Draft pinlist JSON schema and validation script (ajv)
Inventory current TF modules and providers used by private deployments
Populate initial compatibility matrix mapping current deployed module versions to provider versions
Create GH Actions workflow to validate pinlist and run canary applies
Add health_checks.sh that verifies KV cache priming, API handshake latency, routing, TLS cert rotation, and basic inference smoke tests
Write PR template and upgrade runbook; add to docs site
Coordinate Security/Compliance for artifact signing and KMS integration
risks: Provider major version bumps can break native provider behavior (state schema changes). Module changes that rely on provider behavior must be tested in an isolated environment before rollout. Risk of blocking security patches if pinning is too strict — mitigated by auto-patch policy for non-breaking patches.
open_questions: Should we allow minor provider bumps without manual approval if tests pass? (Proposed: allow if compatibility matrix lists 'minor: auto' and tests pass)
Which team owns the pinlist PR approvals for emergency security patches? (Ops vs Platform)
How often should we run a scheduled compatibility sweep (monthly / quarterly)?
